intended_object: A presentation ⟨X | R⟩ of a group G: a generating family X → G together with a set R of relators in the free group F(X), such that the kernel of the induced surjection F(X) → G is the normal closure of R, so that G ≅ F(X)/⟨⟨R⟩⟩. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is faithful. `Generators G ι` contains a map `val : ι → G` whose image generates `G`. This is exactly the condition that the canonical map `FreeGroup.lift val : F(ι) → G` is surjective. `Presentation` adds a set of relators `rel ⊆ F(ι)` and requires `ker(lift) = normalClosure rel`. That is the textbook definition of a group presentation (for example Holt–Rees–Röver, §1).

The library itself proves `presentedGroupEquiv : PresentedGroup P.rel ≃* G`, which confirms that this is the intended notion. Degenerate cases also behave correctly:
- an empty `ι` presents the trivial group;
- an empty `rel` means `G` is free on the family.

The setting is already the natural one: `G` is any group and `ι` is any index type. Mathlib's `PresentedGroup` is related but different: it builds the quotient group F(ι)/⟨⟨rel⟩⟩ from relators. It does not package a presentation of a given group `G`. So there is no more general existing counterpart, and the definition is not too narrow.
